.... FOURTH INNINGS ...

A job well done by Zimbabwe! Speaking at the post-Day 3 press conference, Blessing Muzarabani had mentioned that they would ideally want to restrict the lead to under 200 and his side has done just that, with Muzarabani himself leading the charge. Bangladesh began the day with a lead of 112, but could only manage to add 61 more runs before being bowled out.

OUT! CAUGHT! THAT WILL BE THE END OF BANGLADESH'S INNINGS! Full on off, Jaker Ali shuffles across a bit and goes for the slog sweep. He gets a lot of air on that one but not the distance, as the deep mid-wicket fielder gets under the high ball and gobbles it up near the boundary. That is a good catch from Nick Welch near the boundary. Blessing Muzarabani finishes with a six-fer to his name. And Zimbabwe have a target of 174 runs!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! The first half hour went Zimbabwe's way as they picked up three quick wickets to jolt Bangladesh early. UPDATE - 4.27 am GMT - Good news! The match officials are satisfied with the ground conditions, and if there’s no further rain, play is set to commence at 5 am GMT. Here are the revised session timings for the day. The first session will run from 5 am GMT to 7 am GMT, followed by the second session, which will commence at 7.40 am GMT and continue until 9.40 am GMT. The third and final session of the day will start at 10 am GMT and conclude at 11.45 am GMT. Of course, all these timings are subject to weather and light conditions permitting. Let’s hope for uninterrupted play.

UPDATE - 4.18 am GMT - The ground staff continue to work tirelessly to get the field ready, but a patch down the ground remains a major area of concern. We are still awaiting the result of the inspection. We will keep you posted.

UPDATE - 3.37 am GMT - Well, we are hearing that there will be a delayed start to Day 4. It is not raining at the moment, but heavy overnight rain has left the outfield damp, and the ground staff need more time to get the ground ready for play. An inspection will take place at 4 am GMT. Stay tuned.

Zimbabwe will feel that they should have taken a wicket or two more, with the kind of assistance available from the pitch, especially their spinners, who failed to take wickets, as the home side ended the day with their noses ahead. So, the visitors will look for some early inroads and would want to restrict Bangladesh under a lead of 200. On the other hand, for Bangladesh, they would want this current partnership to flourish more. The presence of captain Najmul Hossain Shanto will give them a lot of confidence, but the margin for error will be less, as they are just two wickets away from getting into the tailenders. So, stick around, as the first ball on day 4 is not far away.

Bangladesh won a major part of Day 3, as they wiped out the remaining deficit and got into the lead with minimal damage. Mahmudul Hasan Joy fell at the start of the day, adding just five runs to his overnight total. Then we saw a healthy partnership of 65 runs between captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mominul Haque as the home side got into the lead. After that, Mushfiqur Rahim, too, fell early as the home side was reduced to an effective score of 73/4. In the 3rd session, though, Jaker Ali and Najmul Hossain Shanto batted with caution and put away anything loose, as they both stitched together an unbeaten 39-run stand before bad light stopped play.

Hello, one and all, and welcome to Day 4 of the opening test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium. Yesterday, only 44 overs were bowled as rain had a major say, as the first session was washed out. Today, too, rain is expected to play a bit of a spoilsport as the weather forecast reads. Bangladesh are currently leading by 112 runs with 6 wickets in hand, and one feels that the home team is slightly ahead, as they will be bowling last on this bowling-friendly wicket. However, the visitors won’t be disheartened much, as some quick early wickets today can immediately shift the pressure back on the home team. There is enough help from the wicket, and this entire Test match has been a seesaw battle, with the pendulum swinging from one team to the other.
... DAY 4, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, three days of the Test are in the books with two days still to go. Neither side holds a clear advantage at the moment, and both are still jostling to gain the upper hand. Since we lost the entire first session on Day 3 and a good chunk of the final session as well, there’s a possibility of an early start on Day 4 to make up for the lost time. However, the forecast for Day 4 isn’t too encouraging either, with rain predicted once again. Fingers crossed the weather holds up, and we get as much play as possible. Until then, take care and goodbye!

Bangladesh went into the break with a 73-run lead, and Zimbabwe had their tails up. Najmul Hossain Shanto and Jaker Ali then came together and forged a steady partnership, aided in some ways by the ball getting older. The pair extended the lead to 112 runs before bad light brought an abrupt end to the day. As the tourists reflect on the day, they will be left ruing a missed opportunity when the keeper Nyasha Mayavo dropped Shanto on 26.

That's it for the day! It’s STUMPS on Day 3. The moving day promised much more, but rain early on and later bad light allowed only 44 overs of play. The first session was washed out, but the next two sessions saw an arm-wrestle unfold. Zimbabwe made a strong start, with Blessing Muzarabani and Richard Ngarava finding the right areas, with Muzarabani striking to dismiss Mahmudul Hasan Joy. Najmul Hossain Shanto responded with positive intent, and suddenly the runs began to flow for the home side. However, Zimbabwe bounced back with a couple of key breakthroughs to finish the session on a high.

We will have to wait and see if there’s any chance of play resuming.

The steep bounce extracted by the tall Zimbabwean pacers has been tough to negotiate for the home side, who now hold a 73-run lead with 6 wickets in hand. A lot will rest on Shanto’s shoulders going forward. Zimbabwe have their tails up and will be eyeing a few quick breakthroughs to tilt the balance further in their favour. Play can continue until 12 pm GMT, provided the light holds up. The third and final session is coming up shortly.

Zimbabwe bossed the early exchanges in the second session as Blessing Muzarabani and Richard Ngarava hit their straps straight away. Mahmudul Hasan Joy fell to the short-ball ploy but Najmul Hossain Shanto made his intentions clear from the get-go and landed a counterpunch with some fluent strokeplay. The change bowlers, Victor Nyauchi and Wessly Madhevere, initially lacked the incision to break through, but Victor eventually managed to find the edge of Mominul Haque to break the partnership.

SESSION SUMMARY - 28.4 overs, 98 runs and 3 wickets. Zimbabwe end the session on a high and will head into the break feeling much better about their position. They thoroughly deserved the rewards for their disciplined bowling, with Blessing Muzarabani standing out once again. Bangladesh, on the other hand, will be gutted to have lost Mushfiqur Rahim right on the stroke of Tea. The hosts now have it all to do when they return for the final session.

UPDATE - 6.05 am GMT - We have a start time, folks. Play on Day 3 will commence at 7 am GMT. With that, LUNCH has been taken. The entire first session was washed out, but with improved conditions, we are hopeful for uninterrupted play in the next couple of sessions. TEA will be taken at 9.20 am GMT, and play can be extended until 12 pm GMT to make up for the lost time, provided the light permits.

UPDATE - 5.49 am GMT - More promising signs! The covers are off, and the skies have brightened considerably. The ground staff are working away, and as long as the rain stays away, we could be inching closer to some action. Stay tuned!

UPDATE - 5.30 am GMT - Good news! It has stopped raining, and the ground staff are out to get the mop-up operation going. While the venue is known for its excellent drainage, only the square was covered, and with the amount of rain we have had, it is going to take a fair bit of time to get the outfield ready. As things stand, it’s safe to say that any play will only be possible after the first session. We will keep you posted with further updates.

UPDATE - 5.02 am GMT - The waiting game continues in Sylhet! It's still coming down steadily, the covers are firmly in place, and the overcast skies are showing no signs of clearing. The outfield is taking a soaking and, for now, there's no movement from the ground staff either.

UPDATE - 4.40 am GMT - Not much has changed since the last update. The rain persists, and water has begun to pool on the covers, which is understandable given the overnight showers and the persistent rain throughout the morning. The wait, unfortunately, continues.
UPDATE - 4.06 am GMT - It continues to rain steadily in Sylhet. Given the gloomy forecast, we could be in for a bit of a wait. Stay with us for further updates!

UPDATE - 3.49 am GMT - Well, not the most ideal start to Day 3. There's been persistent drizzle this morning in Sylhet, and overnight rain hasn’t helped matters either. The covers are on, and we will likely have a delayed start unless things clear up quickly. Stay tuned!

The Bangladeshi batters did well in the last hour as they lost only 1 wicket in that tricky part and batted with a lot of intent, putting away anything loose. So, the visitors will look for some early wickets in the all-important first session, whereas Bangladeshi batters will look to continue the positive intent they showcased in the last hour yesterday. It’s going to be a day where one team might just surge ahead in the game. The action on Day 3 coming up shortly!

After a rather underwhelming performance on Day 1, the home side made a good comeback as they started hitting the straps from the first session, with the pacers cleaning up the top order. However, a gritty fifty from Sean Williams and some very useful contributions from the lower order helped the visitors get into the lead, as they dominated the 2nd session in particular. A late spin web from Mehidy Hasan Miraz ensured the lead stayed under 100, as he ended up with a fifer to his name, wrapping up the Zimbabwean innings on 273.

Hello, one and all, and welcome to Day 3 of the opening Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium. It’s what we call the moving day of the Test match. This Test hangs right in the balance as Bangladesh are just 25 runs behind, with 9 wickets in hand. The visitors might feel they are slightly ahead, as they took an 82-run lead in the first innings, but they will be wary of the fact that they have to bat last on this wicket that has seen variable bounce at times.

10 wickets on Day 1, 11 wickets on Day 2 - What does Day 3 have in store for us? For Bangladesh, it will be about seeing off the first hour and taking it from there, as we saw batting becoming easier, particularly in the second session. For Zimbabwe, they will be batting last, so they will need to be on their game with the ball and in the field, making sure they hold onto every chance that comes their way. Day 3 promises to be yet another entertaining day, with the first ball to be bowled at 4 am GMT. See you then. Cheers!

Towards the back end of the third session, the Bangladeshi openers had their work cut out against the Zimbabwean pace attack. Shadman Islam couldn’t see it through to the close of play, but his opening partner, Mahmudul Hasan Joy, who was dropped on 6, managed to see the day off. Alongside Mominul Haque, they chipped away at the deficit and were quick to put away the bad balls, something they will need to continue doing when they return on Day 3.

After failing to make the most of the conditions late on Day 1, Bangladesh certainly corrected course in the morning session. Nahid Rana and Hasan Mahmud set the tone early, and the dismissal of Brian Bennett brought a noticeable spring to the hosts’ step. Sean Williams and Wessly Madhevere came together to steady the innings and began the rebuilding job, but a rush of blood led to Williams' downfall just after nudging Zimbabwe into the lead. At that point, it looked like Bangladesh would barge through the rest of the batting line-up, but that wasn’t to be. The tail frustrated the hosts, stretching the lead to 82 runs.

SESSION SUMMARY - 29.2 overs, 117 runs and 5 wickets. An absorbing day of Test cricket where the teams traded punches, but at the end of it all, the game stands finely poised going into Day 3. Bangladesh finished the day on a high after conceding a lead, while Zimbabwe will be disappointed not to have picked up more than one wicket and for allowing the hosts to score at a fair clip.
